name: Pout
blurb: Pushed-out lips and puffed cheeks: the sulky, mock-annoyed face of cute characters
title: Pout Expression: Puffed Cheeks, Sulky Faces & Drawing Reference
description: Pout expression reference: puffed-cheek sulks, kissy pouts and duck face, how to draw pushed-out lips in anime style, and how to pout naturally in photos.
answer: A pout is a facial expression where the lips push forward or press together, often with puffed cheeks and lowered brows. It shows mild sulking or mock annoyance, and in anime it is a classic way to make a character look childishly cross without being truly angry.

sections.h: Why the pout reads as cute
body: Real anger tightens the face; a pout exaggerates it into something rounder and softer. Cheeks fill with air, the mouth becomes a small bump, and the eyes look away or up from under the brows. The message is "I am upset, and I want you to notice", which makes it endearing rather than threatening.
In Japanese manga the puffed-cheek anime pout is often lettered with the sound effect puku, and it suits tsundere characters, younger siblings and anyone who loses a small argument.

ul: Puffed-cheek pout: cheeks inflated, lips pressed into a short line or tiny triangle; the classic sulk.
Lip pout: lower lip pushed out, chin dimpled, eyes wet; closer to about to cry.
Kissy pout: lips rounded forward as if blowing a kiss; playful rather than sulky.
Duck face: lips pushed out with cheeks sucked in, popular in early 2010s selfies.
Side-eye pout: head turned away, eyes sliding back toward the viewer, arms often crossed.

body: Start with the cheek outline: in a puffed pout the jaw line bulges outward between the cheekbone and the mouth corner, so the face becomes rounder at the bottom. Draw the mouth small and close to the nose, either as a wavy line or a tiny upturned triangle.

Angle the brows down toward the nose but keep the eyes large; narrow eyes push the face toward real anger. A blush across the cheeks, a sweat drop or a small cross-shaped vein mark at the temple are common comedic additions. In profile, the lips should project past the line of the nose tip only slightly; too far looks like whistling.

sections.h: Posing a pouting face for photos
body: Take a breath, hold a little air in the cheeks, and relax the forehead. Looking slightly up at a camera held above eye level enlarges the eyes and keeps the pout soft.

Add one prop or gesture to give the sulk a reason: crossed arms, hugging a plush, or poking a puffed cheek with one finger. Keep the shoulders loose, because tense shoulders turn a cute pout into a stiff one.

faq.q: What is the puffed cheek face called?
faq.a: In English it is usually called a pout or puffed cheeks. In Japanese manga the effect is often lettered puku or pukū.

faq.q: Is a pout the same as duck face?
faq.a: No. A pout usually shows sulking, often with puffed cheeks, while duck face pushes the lips out and sucks the cheeks in for a posed selfie look.

faq.q: How do I pout without looking angry?
faq.a: Keep the eyes open and soft and only the brows slightly lowered. Narrowed eyes and a clenched jaw make it read as real anger.
